title: Wind Tunnel
tagline: A real 2-D fluid solver driving a colour-field animation — nothing on screen is keyframed.
method: Two solvers share one interface. `lbm.py` is a D2Q9 lattice-Boltzmann scheme with a BGK collision operator and a Smagorinsky LES term, using half-way bounce-back on a boolean mask so any closed polygon becomes a wall with no meshing step; a moving-wall term lets that mask change every step. `cns.py` is a compressible finite-volume Navier-Stokes solver — MUSCL reconstruction with a minmod limiter, an HLLC Riemann solver at every face, SSP-RK2 in time, plus viscous stress and Fourier conduction — which gives you temperature, internal energy and genuine shock capture. The velocity field is colour-mapped and overlaid with streaklines integrated backwards from their current positions, then piped as raw RGB24 to ffmpeg.

output.note: The aspect ratio is a render setting, not a property of the solver — `RenderConfig` takes any `nx`/`ny`, and `--flow up|down|right` chooses which lattice axis becomes the screen's long one. A 16:9 landscape tunnel is `--flow right` at a wider `RenderConfig`.

modules.what: D2Q9 lattice-Boltzmann, BGK + Smagorinsky LES. Half-way bounce-back on a boolean mask with a moving-wall term. Tunnel mode (inlet, zero-gradient outlet + sponge, free-slip sides) or `closed=True` for a sealed box. Carries `set_inlet`, `set_farfield`, `set_drive` (scalar or per-cell), `set_wall_velocity`, `set_inlet_turbulence`, `force_field`, `perturb`, `health`.

Compressible Navier-Stokes, finite volume. MUSCL + minmod, HLLC fluxes, SSP-RK2, explicit viscous stress and conduction at Pr 0.71, Smagorinsky. A real ideal gas at gamma = 1.4. Body by ghost-cell immersed boundary on the same mask. Validated against the exact Sod solution and oblique-shock theory.

Free bodies the flow actually moves. `FreeBody` reads the momentum the fluid handed its surface, adds gravity and buoyancy, and integrates Newton-Euler. `BodySystem` owns per-body masks, the wall-velocity field, soft contacts, soft walls, containment, optional central and pairwise gravity, and liquid coalescence.

Bodies as closed polygons in unit-chord space, plus `place`/`rasterize` to put them on a lattice at any scale and angle. `image_body` traces a polygon straight out of a PNG alpha channel, so any silhouette becomes a solid.

Transported coloured species. One D2Q5 BGK lattice per species, advected by the fluid's own velocity and sharing its bounce-back, so dye and flow can never disagree about where the solid is. Diffusivity is kept tiny, so the mixing you see is the mixing the flow does.

The white dashes. Tails are integrated backwards from the current position every frame rather than kept as history, which means tail length is a free parameter and a respawn never desyncs. Particles die of a randomised age and respawn uniformly.

256-entry LUTs: `jet`, `turbo`, `ice`, `inferno`, `vort`, `blues`, `reds`. The `blues`/`reds` pair track each other's stop luminances entry for entry, so swapping palette needs no re-tuning of `vmax` or `gamma`.

`Tunnel` — the simulation-plus-compositor object — and the `render_scene`/`render_stills` drivers. Owns the lattice-to-screen mapping, the frame clock, the ffmpeg pipe, the divergence guard, and the optional HUD/legend overlays.
`RenderConfig`: everything tunable. `nx`/`ny` (simulated) and `vis_*` (visible window) derive from `flow`, `scale` and `overscan`. NVENC probe with automatic libx264 fallback, and ffmpeg resolution.
CuPy backend with automatic numpy fallback. Scrubs a stale `CUDA_PATH` for the process only, so a system pinned to an older toolkit does not break the JIT.
Scene-side rigging helpers — the small amount of bookkeeping that sits between a composition and the solver.

Bridge to the CRT film filter in the oscilloscope engine, handed a neutral white-phosphor config. Mandatory here: the green-phosphor defaults are only correct for a single-hue trace and would wreck a full-colour field.
The compressible solver against the exact Sod shock-tube solution.
Measured oblique-shock angle and post-shock state against the theta-beta-Mach relation.
Whether a clip built as a loop actually loops — compares first and last frame numerically.
Lattice-to-physical calibration: what a chosen `u0`, chord and Reynolds number actually mean in cells and steps.

objects.intro: Every one returns a closed polygon in unit-chord space. `place(pts, chord, cx, cy, aoa_deg, pivot)` scales, rotates about the quarter-chord and translates it; `rasterize(polys, nx, ny, supersample=2)` turns a list of them into the boolean mask the solvers take. Because the mask is re-made from scratch each step, a body can move, rotate or change shape with no meshing anywhere.

items.name: naca4
items.what: Any NACA 4-digit section from its code.
items.notes: '0012' for symmetric, '2412' for the cambered reference section.

items.name: circle
items.what: Unit-diameter cylinder.
items.notes: The von Karman vortex-street case; the standard 2-D solver validation body.

items.name: square
items.what: Square plate.
items.notes: Unlike a disc it feels a torque, so a free one tumbles.

items.name: plate
items.what: Thin flat plate.
items.notes: The dynamic-stall body — sharp leading edge, so separation is fixed and not Reynolds-dependent.

items.name: wedge
items.what: Wedge, apex forward.
items.notes: The oblique-shock generator on the compressible solver.

items.name: wedge_rev
items.what: Wedge, flat face forward.
items.notes: Bluff-body counterpart — the drag comparison against `wedge`.

items.name: ellipse
items.what: Ellipse at any thickness ratio.
items.notes: The continuous knob between `circle` and `plate`.

items.name: teardrop
items.what: Rounded nose, tapered tail.
items.notes: Streamlined bluff body; the low-drag end of a shape tour.

items.name: turbofan
items.what: A 2-D section through a ducted jet engine. Returns a dict — `cowl`, `spinner`, and the radius closures `duct_r`/`spin_r`/`outer_r`/`r_out` — not a single polygon.
items.notes: Two mirrored cowl halves make a real duct the flow passes THROUGH. The radius closures let a composition find the free passage without restating the constants. Its docstring records the two silhouettes that were tried first and read wrong.

items.name: surfboard
items.signature: surfboard(width=0.28, tail=0.36, tip=0.012, nose_p=0.70, x_n=0.12, n=240)
items.what: Planing hull section — nose rocker, tail width and tip thickness all parameterised.
items.notes: Paired with `board_texture` for the drawn deck.

items.name: board_texture
items.what: Generates a deck/rail/stringer texture bitmap for a drawn board.
items.notes: Cosmetic only — carries no physics.

items.name: cow
items.what: A cow silhouette, as a closed polygon.
items.notes: Not a joke: it is the bluff-body extreme in a shape comparison, and it is the readability test for `image_body`.

items.name: metaball
items.what: Smooth-union outline of a set of circles, found by radial bisection.
items.notes: The merging-droplet shape. Pair with `bodies.droplet` for an area-conserving version.

items.name: image_body
items.signature: image_body(path, cells=120.0, flip_x=False, close_cells=1.5, detail=3.0, alpha_thr=128)
items.what: Traces a closed polygon from a PNG's alpha channel — any silhouette becomes a solid body.
items.notes: The general escape hatch: if you can draw it, the solver can put flow round it.

items.name: place
items.signature: place(pts, chord, cx, cy, aoa_deg=0.0, pivot=0.25)
items.what: Scale, rotate about the pivot chord fraction, translate.
items.notes: Size bodies against the SCREEN, never against a lattice axis — which axis is 'across the picture' flips with `--flow`.

items.name: rasterize
items.what: Polygons to the boolean solid mask.
items.notes: Supersampled by default so a rotating body does not jitter cell by cell.

objects.intro: Objects the flow moves, rather than objects held in place. A composition may choose a body's position at time t, its material, or a prescribed spin — and then it must let go. Every trajectory below that is solved.

items.name: FreeBody
items.signature: FreeBody(profile, size, x, y, *, name, ang, vx, vy, ...)
items.what: One rigid body. Reads the momentum the fluid handed its surface, adds gravity and buoyancy, integrates Newton-Euler.
items.notes: `smooth` low-passes the fluid load; without it the body chatters on lattice noise.

items.name: BodySystem
items.signature: BodySystem(nx, ny, g=5e-4, floor=0.055, ceiling=0.985, wall_gap=7.0, ...)
items.what: Owns every body: masks, the wall-velocity field, soft contacts, soft walls, containment, central and pairwise gravity, coalescence.
items.notes: Modes are `dynamic` (bodies respond) and `tracer` (bodies follow the flow).

items.name: density_for_fall
items.signature: density_for_fall(profile_name, size, v_fall, u0, g, unit_area)
items.what: Solves the terminal-velocity balance for the density that makes a body fall at a chosen speed.
items.notes: This is how you choose what a body is MADE OF instead of scripting its path.

items.name: droplet
items.what: Area-conserving metaball outline.
items.notes: A shape that changes must change smoothly and at constant area, or the solver sees a mass source.

items.name: set_profile
items.what: Re-derives mass, inertia and radius when a body's shape changes mid-clip.

items.name: spin
items.what: Prescribed rotation — a motor turning a cylinder rather than the flow doing it.
items.notes: Opts the body out of the surface-speed cap, so the composition then owns that budget itself.

objects.intro: The legitimate ways to push the fluid. All of them are things a real rig has.

items.name: set_inlet
items.what: The inflow condition — uniform, or any spanwise profile.
items.notes: Whenever this is far from uniform you must also call `set_farfield`, or the sponge pulls the flow back toward a freestream that no longer exists.

items.name: set_farfield
items.what: Retargets the outlet sponge to a spanwise profile.
items.notes: The partner to a non-uniform `set_inlet`.

items.name: set_drive
items.what: Drives the fluid toward a target velocity. `beta` may be a scalar or a per-cell field.
items.notes: A per-cell beta is what makes a localised stirrer possible. Velocity fields SUPERPOSE — sum the components and take max() of the masks; weight-averaging overlapping patches drives the fluid between them toward a target that is too slow.

items.name: set_wall_velocity
items.what: Moving-wall term for bounce-back.
items.notes: Breaks above |u_wall| ~ 0.12. Keep body speeds small and buy apparent speed with `steps`.

items.name: set_inlet_turbulence
items.what: Continuous divergence-free freestream turbulence, convected as a frozen field.
items.notes: This is what makes air noisy for a whole run rather than kicked once at t=0.

items.name: force_field
items.what: Per-cell wall force — the momentum the fluid gave the solid.
items.notes: Lives on the fluid cells BESIDE the body, never on its own cells. Getting this wrong once measured Cd ~ 22 against a textbook 1.2.

items.name: init_velocity
items.what: Seeds the domain's initial field.
items.notes: In a sealed box, seed at REST — the default fills the domain with a uniform freestream, which in a closed pool is a slab of water sliding sideways for the whole clip.

items.name: health
items.what: One scalar reporting solve stability.
items.notes: A stable solve and a CORRECT one are different questions. This answers only the first.

items.name: jet
items.what: The default speed palette.

items.name: turbo
items.what: Perceptually improved rainbow.

items.name: ice
items.what: Cool monotone.

items.name: inferno
items.what: Dark-to-hot monotone.

items.name: vort
items.what: Diverging map for signed vorticity.
items.notes: Use with `--field vort`; zero must sit at the midpoint.

items.name: blues
items.what: Blue shades only, built for a near-zero field.
items.notes: The still-water palette — a normal map puts a dead pool at one flat colour.

items.name: reds
items.what: The same ramp, hue-rotated.
items.notes: Stop luminances track `blues` entry for entry, so a composition swaps palette without re-tuning `vmax`/`gamma`.

scenes_intro: The compositions themselves are not in this repository — see the README. They are listed because the list is the useful part: each one is a different answer to what you can point this solver at, and each has frames beside it. `rocket_engine` is withheld at the author's request.

parameters_intro: The handful of numbers that decide whether a solve is stable, and the one relationship that breaks more solves than anything else.

parameters.name: u0
parameters.meaning: Under `lbm` this is a LATTICE VELOCITY. Under `cns` the identical field is a MACH NUMBER, because the solver is built with c_inf = 1. This is the single most dangerous trap in the project.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.meaning: Solver steps per output frame at 60 fps, scaled by 60/fps with a fractional accumulator. Apparent speed = lattice speed x steps/frame.
parameters.range: 40–120. ALWAYS buy apparent speed here, never by raising u0.

parameters.name: re
parameters.meaning: Chord Reynolds number. Sets the relaxation time; low Re is thick and syrupy, high Re sheds finer structure and needs a finer lattice.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.meaning: Lattice cells per screen pixel. `--preview` halves the frame size AND this, so the lattice — and therefore the physics — is identical to the final.

parameters.name: overscan
parameters.meaning: Pads the simulated domain beyond the visible frame on every side. Bodies enter and leave off-camera, an appearing body's pressure transient decays before it reaches the picture, and a sealed box's walls sit outside the shot.

parameters.name: flow
parameters.meaning: Which lattice axis becomes the screen's long one: `up` (wake gets the full height), `down` (subject at top, effect below), `right` (classic landscape tunnel).
parameters.range: All three are orientation-preserving on purpose — a naive 'x down, y right' would be a reflection and every vortex would spin the wrong way.

parameters.name: settle
parameters.meaning: Seconds of flow run before frame 0, so the clip opens on an established field rather than a transient.

parameters.name: wall_gap
parameters.meaning: Stand-off distance for soft walls and contacts.
parameters.range: Never let any gap go sub-cell. A hard clamp steps a body's wall velocity in one tick and the boundary broadcasts it as a visible ripple across the frame.

parameters.name: speed_gain
parameters.meaning: Keys streakline brightness to local speed.
parameters.range: ~1.0 for still water — it is what makes the dashes appear only where the water actually moves
